title: The Last Verdict Anew
premise: Vesper Voss, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent three years cataloguing the quiet sins of Hollow Creek, receives two letters on the same morning: one confessing to a thirty-year-old drowning, the other promising a second death before the town's anniversary dinner. As he cross-references old dispatch logs and taxi manifests, he discovers the original 'accident' was witnessed from his own cab company's back seat — and that someone inside the dinner committee is silencing witnesses. At the anniversary toast, Vesper exposes the killer, the town's beloved founder's daughter, but chooses not to hand over the letter that would also condemn his mentor, paying the price of survival by carrying a secret of his own at last.
about_author: Sable Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent a decade listening to confessions never meant for the record. She writes mysteries about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Postmark
chapters.summary: Vesper Voss, working the graveyard shift at Hollow Creek Taxi, opens two letters postmarked the same day: one confessing to the 1994 drowning of councilman Aldous Pike, one promising 'the second name' before the anniversary dinner. His POV establishes his filing system of secrets. Emotional beat: unease — the letters know things only a dispatcher would recognize.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Vesper searches his three-year archive of dispatch logs and finds gaps where rides to Pike's lake house should appear. POV shifts briefly to retired dispatcher Marge Kettle, who warns him to stop looking. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of belonging to something finally bigger than his shift.

chapters.title: What the Back Seat Saw
chapters.summary: Vesper learns a Hollow Creek cab carried four passengers to the lake the night Pike drowned; the fare was paid in cash by Corinne Ashe, now head of the anniversary committee. Her POV shows her rehearsing a toast while burning an old photograph. Emotional beat: cold calculation beneath civic warmth.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Vesper interviews the surviving dinner guests, each with airtight alibis that share one flaw: they all called the same taxi company that night. His POV. Emotional beat: frustration curdling into suspicion that the conspiracy is structural, not personal.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: A second promise arrives naming its victim: Marge Kettle. Vesper races to her house and finds her alive but drugged, her archive ransacked. Marge's POV reveals she wrote neither letter — she received them too, years ago. Emotional beat: terror and betrayal.

chapters.title: Fares Paid in Silence
chapters.summary: Following money trails, Vesper discovers the taxi company's founder was bribed into falsifying logs in 1994 — and that his own mentor, dispatcher Emory Hale, inherited the hush money. Vesper's POV. Emotional beat: grief, as belonging curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Corinne manipulates the seating chart to isolate Vesper, offering him a job and a place in town if he returns the letters. Her POV shows power corrupting even her genuine affection for him. Emotional beat: seduction and threat braided together.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Last Round
chapters.summary: On the eve of the dinner, Vesper reconstructs the full route of the 1994 cab ride and realizes the second promised death is Corinne's own staged martyrdom to bury the truth forever. His POV. Emotional beat: clarity arriving too late to stop the machinery already in motion.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the anniversary dinner, Corinne poisons the punch meant for herself and frames Marge; Vesper interrupts the toast, playing the original dispatch tape over the hall speakers. Climax: her confession spills out before the whole town. Emotional beat: cathartic exposure, ugly and public.

chapters.title: Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Vesper holds the letter implicating Emory in the cover-up. He files it unopened in his alphabet of secrets, taking his first true place among the town's keepers. Resolution: justice served, price paid, belonging purchased. Emotional beat: bittersweet complicity.
